show: Peace Over Panic: Life Beyond Anxiety
titel: Therapy Isn’t Working, Now What? Finding the Right Treatment for OCD and Health Anxiety

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Why standard therapy often fails for OCD and health anxiety and what actually works
kurzfassung: Many people struggling with OCD and health anxiety spend years in traditional talk therapy without seeing improvement because it can inadvertently reinforce the cycle. Specialist Gracie Block explains how evidence-based approaches like Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) help patients break free by learning to tolerate uncertainty. The discussion highlights the importance of finding properly trained clinicians and offers practical guidance for navigating treatment.
stichpunkte: OCD and health anxiety are frequently misdiagnosed, with patients often waiting years to receive appropriate care.
Traditional talk therapy and endless reassurance-seeking can act as compulsions that worsen the anxiety cycle.
Health anxiety involves a desperate drive to figure out physical sensations immediately, creating rigid life rules.
Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is considered the gold standard psychological treatment for OCD.
ERP combines systematically confronting feared situations with preventing safety behaviors and avoidance.
The ultimate goal of treatment is not to eliminate all fear, but to build tolerance for uncertainty and live a full life.
Finding a specialist specifically trained in ERP and acceptance-based modalities is crucial for effective recovery.

clips.hook: It takes an average of nine to 14 years to get a proper diagnosis.
clips.text: Getting an accurate diagnosis for obsessive-compulsive disorder or health anxiety typically requires nearly a decade and a half.

clips.hook: Trying to figure it out immediately keeps the anxiety cycle alive.
clips.text: An urgent mental drive to resolve physical uncertainties right away reinforces the underlying threat response.

clips.hook: Standard CBT structures exposure work to help confront social anxiety.
clips.text: Cognitive behavioral interventions utilize systematic behavioral plans to gradually reintroduce patients to avoided social settings.

clips.hook: Are you willing to take the risk of a cardiac event to get your life back?
clips.text: Recovery requires stepping into daily activities while accepting the impossibility of absolute safety regarding physical health.

You notice an unusual sensation, and your mind immediately goes to the worst-case scenario. You Google your symptoms, check your body, ask for reassurance, or schedule another appointment. Even when you’re told everything is okay, the relief doesn’t last.
Then you try therapy, but you still don’t feel better. Does that mean you’re broken, or could you simply be receiving the wrong kind of treatment?
In this episode of Peace Over Panic, Taylor sits down with Gracie Block, a Licensed Professional Counselor at Dallas CBT, to explore the close relationship between OCD and health anxiety and why treating these conditions requires specialized knowledge.
Gracie explains the cycle of intrusive fears, compulsive behaviors, temporary relief, and renewed doubt. She also breaks down Exposure and Response Prevention, or ERP, an evidence-based treatment for OCD that helps people face uncertainty while reducing the checking, avoidance, and reassurance-seeking behaviors that keep anxiety alive.
Taylor also shares her own experiences with health anxiety, feeling misunderstood in therapy, turning cognitive exercises into another source of reassurance, and eventually recognizing that an unsuccessful therapy experience did not mean she was incapable of getting better.

About Gracie Block
Gracie Block is a Licensed Professional Counselor at Dallas CBT. She works with children, adolescents, young adults, and families experiencing OCD, anxiety, depression, trauma, and emotional dysregulation.
Her approach incorporates Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Exposure and Response Prevention, Dialectical Behavior Therapy, and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy. Gracie brings both professional expertise and personal understanding to her work with OCD and anxiety.
